record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.context_brief: coupled equations for optimal static output feedback
record.original_question: Understand the existence, uniqueness, and qualitative solution properties of the coupled matrix equations (6.24)-(6.25) that characterize optimal static output feedback when only partial noise-free measurements y(t) = C x(t) are available. Equivalently, solve the underlying optimal static output-feedback problem in a way that clarifies when the coupled equations admit meaningful positive semidefinite solutions.

evidence.quote: Although (6.24) and (6.25) provide a transparent and elegant generalization of (6.8), it is a remarkable fact that virtually nothing is known about their solution properties.
Hence, these two unsolved problems go hand in hand.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the linear time-invariant stochastic system
  dx(t)/dt = A x(t) + B u(t) + w(t),  y(t) = C x(t),
where x(t) ∈ ℝⁿ is the state, u(t) ∈ ℝᵐ is the control input, y(t) ∈ ℝᵖ is the measured output (a noise-free partial measurement), and w(t) is zero-mean white noise with intensity V = Vᵀ ≥ 0. Let Q = Qᵀ ≥ 0 and R = Rᵀ > 0 be given weighting matrices, and assume (A,B) is stabilizable and (A,C) is detectable.

Consider the static output feedback control law u(t) = K y(t), K ∈ ℝ^{m×p}, and the associated infinite-horizon quadratic cost
  J(K) = lim_{t→∞} E[ x(t)ᵀ Q x(t) + u(t)ᵀ R u(t) ],
defined whenever A + BKC is Hurwitz.

Standard first-order necessary conditions for K to minimize J over the set of stabilizing static output-feedback gains take the form of the coupled matrix equations
  (E1)  0 = (A + BKC)ᵀ P + P (A + BKC) + Q + Cᵀ Kᵀ R K C,
  (E2)  0 = (A + BKC) S + S (A + BKC)ᵀ + V,
  (E3)  0 = R K C S Cᵀ − Bᵀ P S Cᵀ,
in the unknowns P = Pᵀ ≥ 0, S = Sᵀ ≥ 0, and K ∈ ℝ^{m×p}.

Problem. Establish a complete theory of these coupled equations:
(a) Give verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions on (A, B, C, Q, R, V) under which the system (E1)–(E3) admits a solution (P, S, K) with P, S positive semidefinite and A + BKC Hurwitz.
(b) Characterize uniqueness, multiplicity, and the structure of the solution set, and determine which solutions correspond to the global minimum of J(K).
(c) Equivalently, solve the underlying optimal static output-feedback problem: characterize the existence, uniqueness, and qualitative properties of a globally optimal stabilizing gain K* minimizing J(K), and relate K* to solutions of (E1)–(E3).
artifact.category_tag: Static output feedback / coupled matrix Riccati–Lyapunov equations
artifact.status_search_result: The optimal static output feedback problem and the associated coupled Riccati–Lyapunov optimality equations are widely regarded as a long-standing open problem in control theory. Existing literature provides only sufficient conditions, iterative/homotopy algorithms, and special-case results (e.g., LMI-based or guaranteed-cost formulations), but no complete characterization of existence, uniqueness, or global optimality is known.

status_evidence.title: Static Output Feedback: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: The static output feedback problem is one of the most important open questions in control engineering.
status_evidence.claim: Static output feedback is identified as a major open problem in control.

status_evidence.title: Robust decentralized static output feedback
status_evidence.snippet: Coupled Riccati/Lyapunov equations arising in output-feedback synthesis are typically solved iteratively without general existence/uniqueness theory.
status_evidence.claim: Only iterative/sufficient methods exist for the coupled equations.

status_evidence.title: An efficient numerical solution for H2 static output feedback synthesis
status_evidence.snippet: H2 static output feedback synthesis remains numerically challenging, addressed via heuristic/LMI methods.
status_evidence.claim: No closed-form theory; numerical heuristics dominate.
